title: Japanese Conversation & Kana — Beginner Course
designPrinciples: Begin with an explicit learner goal and a short, familiar scene; assume no prior lesson or Japanese knowledge.
Conversation and listening are the goal; scripts and kanji support communication rather than delay it.
Dialogue and phrase text use kana-first Japanese. Do not require romaji; keep it as an optional temporary scaffold.
The three weekly lessons build from noticing meaning, to supported replies, to adapting a conversation.
Local speech, reading, a partner, or self-led practice are alternatives; speech setup never gates a lesson.
Completion records practice and observable evidence, never a claim of fluency or automated speech accuracy.
Follow the broad beginner-to-low-intermediate progression of GENKI I while writing all Kanafish teaching content independently; do not reproduce textbook passages, dialogues, exercises, or audio.

Introduce all core hiragana in Week 1 and katakana in Week 2 as a first pass alongside useful spoken exchanges; practise a few groups at a time and revisit them later. Neither script is a prerequisite for conversation or progress.

reviewCadence.sessionWarmup: Offer a low-pressure revisit only when an earlier lesson is marked practised. If there is no completed lesson, begin with the current goal and new material; never refer to a previous lesson that did not happen.
reviewCadence.weeklyInterleave: At the start of a later week, choose a phrase or line that appeared in a completed lesson from the previous week; if none was practised, teach the current scene instead.
reviewCadence.longerSpacing: Mix in an item from two to four weeks earlier only when a lesson from that week was completed and the item appeared in that lesson. Prefer learner-marked difficult items and change the scene.
reviewCadence.milestoneRevisit: At a checkpoint, invite one earlier conversation function only when it has been practised; keep the main checkpoint on the current milestone.
reviewCadence.adaptation: Introduce review cards after a lesson is completed or after the learner explicitly self-rates an item. First scheduled review is the following day; a missed item returns sooner, while an easy recall waits longer. Review stays optional and unscored.

learningPath.title: Meet people and find your first words
learningPath.outcome: Practise greetings, identity, objects, shopping, routines, and invitations while making a first pass through hiragana and katakana alongside the conversations.

learningPath.title: Describe, travel, and connect actions
learningPath.outcome: Talk about places and past events, describe choices, make simple requests, connect actions, and ask or offer help.

learningPath.title: Talk about people and share stories
learningPath.outcome: Describe people and current activities, then use casual conversation to share preferences and opinions.

learningPath.title: Make plans, share experiences, and get help
learningPath.outcome: Retell past events, compare options, discuss plans and experiences, and explain a health concern with less scripting.

kanaPolicy: Japanese dialogue and phrase text is kana-first. Introduce the full core hiragana set alongside first conversations in Week 1 and the full core katakana set alongside everyday shopping in Week 2 as a first pass, not a one-week mastery deadline. Practise a few groups at a time and revisit them later, including voiced sounds, common contracted combinations, small っ, and the long-vowel mark. Keep kana visible with speech; script recognition never gates a lesson. Topic-specific kanji remain selective recognition cards with kana readings, not handwriting tests.

weeks.title: Meet people and introduce yourself
weeks.canDo: Return a greeting, give a short introduction, and exchange a few facts about name, role, origin, and time.

すみません。

phraseBank.ja: ありがとうございます。
お願いします。
わたしは [なまえ] です。
phraseBank.use: Give your name in a polite introduction.

phraseBank.ja: [くに]じんです。
phraseBank.use: Say your nationality in an introduction.

lessons.title: Greet and give your name
lessons.goal: Say hello back when someone greets you, then offer your name in a short first meeting.
lessons.scene: You meet a new classmate at a community Japanese group. You do not need to understand every word yet; notice the greeting and the names first.

dialogue.speaker: classmate
dialogue.ja: こんにちは。わたしはゆきです。
dialogue.en: Hello. I'm Yuki.

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: こんにちは。わたしはサムです。
dialogue.en: Hello. I'm Sam.

dialogue.speaker: classmate
dialogue.ja: はじめまして。
dialogue.en: Nice to meet you.

listenCheck.question: Which person gives the name Yuki?

responsePractice.prompt: You have just shared your name. Choose a suitable next line.
responsePractice.why: A first meeting is a natural place to say はじめまして.

lessons.sayTask: Return the greeting, say your name, and try a first-meeting phrase once without looking at the English. If you need a moment, use すみません before asking the other person’s name. As a short daily companion practice, read two or three hiragana groups from this week aloud, then find one of those sounds in the conversation.
lessons.adaptation: Change the name and meeting place. Keep the greeting and introduction, then ask the other person’s name.

lessons.title: Ask who someone is
lessons.goal: Ask a new friend a polite yes/no question and give a short positive or negative answer.
lessons.scene: Two people at the group share where they are from and what they do.

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: ゆきさんはがくせいですか。
dialogue.en: Yuki, are you a student?

dialogue.speaker: classmate
dialogue.ja: いいえ、かいしゃいんです。
dialogue.en: No, I'm an office worker.

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: そうですか。わたしもかいしゃいんです。
dialogue.en: I see. I'm an office worker too.

listenCheck.question: What is Yuki’s role?

responsePractice.prompt: You are not a student. Choose the simple polite answer.
choices: いいえ、がくせいじゃないです。
がくせいはどこですか。
meanings: No, I am not a student.
responsePractice.why: じゃないです gives a simple polite negative answer.

lessons.sayTask: Ask whether your partner is a student, then answer with your real or imagined role. As a short daily companion practice, read two or three hiragana groups from this week aloud, then find one of those sounds in the conversation.
lessons.adaptation: Swap student for a job or nationality and use も if the same detail fits both people.
successChecks: Gives a positive or negative answer

lessons.title: Share one more detail
lessons.goal: Use a simple relationship phrase and catch a number or time in a short exchange.
lessons.scene: A classmate asks about your language class and when it starts.

dialogue.speaker: classmate
dialogue.ja: にほんごのクラスはなんじですか。
dialogue.en: What time is Japanese class?

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: ごごいちじです。
dialogue.en: It is at one in the afternoon.

dialogue.speaker: classmate
dialogue.ja: わたしのクラスもごごいちじです。
dialogue.en: My class is at one in the afternoon too.

listenCheck.question: When does the class start?

responsePractice.prompt: Say your class is at 10 in the morning.
responsePractice.why: A short time answer is enough; listen for ごぜん or ごご and the number.

lessons.sayTask: Give one detail about a class, interest, or role, then add a simple time or number. As a short daily companion practice, read two or three hiragana groups from this week aloud, then find one of those sounds in the conversation.
lessons.adaptation: Ask a new question about your partner and use one detail with の or も.

learningTargets: Use polite です sentences, yes/no questions, and simple negative replies to introduce yourself and ask who someone is.
Connect people and details with は・の・も; listen for names, roles, numbers, and a simple time.
Take a first pass through core hiragana; practise a few groups per session and revisit them later. Voiced and contracted sounds are early exposure, not a mastery deadline.

weeks.title: Ask about things and shop
weeks.canDo: Point out an item, ask about its price or owner, and understand a simple location answer.

phraseBank.ja: はじめまして。
わたしは [なまえ] です。
[くに] からきました。
よろしくおねがいします。
phraseBank.en: Pleased to meet you / I look forward to it.

phraseBank.ja: これはいくらですか。
phraseBank.use: Ask about the price of an item near you.

phraseBank.ja: この [もの] はだれのですか。

kanjiCards.whyHere: A useful recognition character on signs and forms about people; no handwriting test.
A practical word likely to appear in an introduction or reservation form.
Recognize a common object label while practising demonstratives.
A useful whole-word recognition item in a shopping scene.

milestone.title: First conversation checkpoint
milestone.task: Give a short self-introduction, ask two familiar questions, and handle one simple object or price question. From five slow, clear prompts, identify the key information in at least four.
evidence: Support used and next practice target

lessons.title: Choose an item nearby
lessons.goal: Use a pointing word to ask about an unfamiliar item and understand its price.
lessons.scene: At a small stationery shop, you point to a notebook on the counter and ask how much it costs.

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: これはいくらですか。
dialogue.en: How much is this?

dialogue.speaker: clerk
dialogue.ja: それはさんびゃくえんです。
dialogue.en: That one is 300 yen.

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: じゃあ、それをください。
dialogue.en: Then I’ll take that, please.

listenCheck.question: How much is the notebook?

responsePractice.prompt: The item is next to the clerk as they listen to you. Which pointing word fits?
responsePractice.why: それ refers to an item near the other person.

lessons.sayTask: Ask the price of one nearby object and choose it or ask about another one. As a short daily companion practice, read two or three katakana groups from this week aloud, then spot one in the shopping conversation.
lessons.adaptation: Change the item and the price. Use これ for something by you and それ for something by the other person.
successChecks: Matches a pointing word to the scene

lessons.title: Ask whose item it is
lessons.goal: Ask about a specific item and say who owns it.
lessons.scene: A friend sees a patterned umbrella beside your chair and asks about it.

dialogue.speaker: friend
dialogue.ja: このかさはだれのですか。
dialogue.en: Whose umbrella is this?

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: わたしのです。
dialogue.en: It is mine.

dialogue.speaker: friend
dialogue.ja: あそこにかばんもありますよ。
dialogue.en: There is a bag over there too.

listenCheck.question: What belongs to the traveller?

responsePractice.prompt: A friend asks whose book this is. Choose your answer.
choices: このほんはいくらですか。
responsePractice.why: の can show a simple possession relationship.

lessons.sayTask: Ask about one object with この and answer using わたしのです or another owner. As a short daily companion practice, read two or three katakana groups from this week aloud, then spot one in the shopping conversation.
lessons.adaptation: Move the object farther away and change この to あの or その as needed.

lessons.title: Compare two choices
lessons.goal: Ask which item fits your need and respond to a short shop suggestion.
lessons.scene: A shop assistant points out two bags and recommends one with a helpful comment.

dialogue.speaker: clerk
dialogue.ja: どのかばんがいいですか。
dialogue.en: Which bag would you like?

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: このかばんがいいです。
dialogue.en: I like this bag.

dialogue.speaker: clerk
dialogue.ja: そのかばん、かるいですよ。
dialogue.en: That bag is light, you know.

listenCheck.question: Which bag does the traveller choose?

responsePractice.prompt: You agree that a suggested item looks good. Choose a natural response.
responsePractice.why: A short agreement keeps a simple shopping exchange moving.

lessons.sayTask: Choose between two things and give one short reason or reaction. As a short daily companion practice, read two or three katakana groups from this week aloud, then spot one in the shopping conversation.
lessons.adaptation: Change the item and choose between これ・それ・あれ or この・その・あの.
successChecks: Catches a short comment with よ

learningTargets: Use これ・それ・あれ・どれ and この・その・あの・どの to point out items and ask whose they are.
Ask about price and location, and notice ね・よ in a short shopping exchange.

Take a first pass through core katakana; practise a few groups per session and revisit them later. Voiced/contracted sounds, ッ, ー, and foreign-word spellings are early exposure, not a mastery deadline.

weeks.title: Talk about routines and make plans
weeks.canDo: Ask about a daily routine, say when and where you do something, and invite someone to join you.

phraseBank.ja: これはなんですか。
[ばしょ] はどこですか。
もういちどおねがいします。
ゆっくりおねがいします。
まいにち、[こと] をします。
いっしょに [こと] しませんか。

kanaFocus: がぎぐげご
ざじずぜぞ
だぢづでど
ばびぶべぼ
ぱぴぷぺぽ
きゃ・しゅ・ちょ

kanjiCards.whyHere: Recognize this common question character; the spoken reading changes with the phrase.
Recognize a common time word in routines.
A practical schedule word; reading support stays in kana.

lessons.title: Ask about a morning routine
lessons.goal: Ask and answer what time someone usually gets up.
lessons.scene: A classmate asks about your morning before a weekend study session.

dialogue.speaker: classmate
dialogue.ja: まいあさ、なんじにおきますか。
dialogue.en: What time do you get up each morning?

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: しちじにおきます。
dialogue.en: I get up at seven.

dialogue.speaker: classmate
dialogue.ja: わたしはろくじはんにおきます。
dialogue.en: I get up at half past six.

listenCheck.question: What time does the traveller get up?

responsePractice.prompt: You get up at 7. Choose the answer.
responsePractice.why: おきます is a polite non-past form for a routine.

lessons.sayTask: Say what time you get up, eat breakfast, or start your day.
lessons.adaptation: Change the time and ask your partner one follow-up about their routine.

lessons.title: Say where you study
lessons.goal: Use a time, an activity, and a place in a short routine description.
lessons.scene: A friend asks where you usually study Japanese after class.

dialogue.speaker: friend
dialogue.ja: どこでにほんごをべんきょうしますか。
dialogue.en: Where do you study Japanese?

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: としょかんでべんきょうします。
dialogue.en: I study at the library.

dialogue.speaker: friend
dialogue.ja: まいにちですか。
dialogue.en: Every day?

listenCheck.question: Where does the traveller study?

responsePractice.prompt: Say you read at home every day.
choices: まいにち、うちでほんをよみます。
まいにち、うちにほんをよみます。
まいにち、うちをほんです。
meanings: I read a book at home every day.
responsePractice.why: で marks the place where an action happens, and を marks the object.

lessons.sayTask: Make one short sentence about an activity, its place, and how often you do it.
lessons.adaptation: Swap the activity and place; try a different frequency such as よく or ときどき.
successChecks: Uses a place for an action

lessons.title: Invite a friend
lessons.goal: Invite someone to do a familiar activity and understand a yes or no reply.
lessons.scene: After class, you ask a classmate to get a drink together.

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: このあと、コーヒーをのみませんか。
dialogue.en: Would you like to have coffee after this?

dialogue.speaker: classmate
dialogue.ja: いいですね。いきましょう。
dialogue.en: That sounds good. Let’s go.

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: じゃあ、えきであいましょう。
dialogue.en: Then let’s meet at the station.

listenCheck.question: Does the classmate accept the invitation?

responsePractice.prompt: Your friend invites you and you would like to go. Choose a reply.
choices: すみません、いけません。
meanings: What time do you get up?
responsePractice.why: いいですね accepts the invitation warmly.

lessons.sayTask: Invite someone to a café, walk, or study session; practise accepting and declining.
lessons.adaptation: Change the activity and place, then ask what time works.

learningTargets: Use polite present/non-past verb forms to talk about habits and everyday actions.
Place time, activity, and location information in a simple sentence using に・で・を.
Ask about routines, use a frequency word, and invite someone with 〜ませんか.
Read familiar kana in short routine words and distinguish time and place details by listening.

weeks.title: Talk about places and past events
weeks.canDo: Say where people or things are, ask what happened, and give a short account of a past day.

phraseBank.ja: コーヒーをください。
メニューをおねがいします。
ここでたべます。
いくらですか。
きのう、[ばしょ] にいきました。
[もの] は [ばしょ] にあります。

kanaFocus: Hiragana review: small っ and long vowels
Katakana: アイウエオ・カキクケコ
Read menu words: コーヒー・メニュー

kanjiCards.whyHere: Recognize the currency character on a menu or price display.
A whole-word recognition item for a past-weekend story.

milestone.title: Places and past-events checkpoint
milestone.task: Locate one person or object, then tell a short account of a past visit. Include one detail from the earlier shopping conversations and catch at least four of five simple details.
evidence: Listening result and next practice target

lessons.title: Find a place in town
lessons.goal: Ask where something is and understand whether a person or thing is there.
lessons.scene: You are looking for a small café near a station and ask a local for help.

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: カフェはどこにありますか。
dialogue.en: Where is the café?

dialogue.speaker: local
dialogue.ja: えきのとなりにあります。
dialogue.en: It is next to the station.

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: ともだちもそこにいますか。
dialogue.en: Is my friend there too?

listenCheck.question: Where is the café?

responsePractice.prompt: Ask where a friend is. Choose the location question.
choices: ゆきさんはどこにいますか。
ゆきさんはなんじですか。
responsePractice.why: います is used for a person or animal in a place.

lessons.sayTask: Ask where one person and one thing are, then repeat the location you hear.
lessons.adaptation: Change the café and station to a shop, a bag, or a friend’s location.
successChecks: Distinguishes a person from a thing

lessons.title: Describe yesterday
lessons.goal: Ask and answer what someone did yesterday using polite past forms.
lessons.scene: A friend asks about your weekend after a day out together.

dialogue.speaker: friend
dialogue.ja: きのうはどうでしたか。
dialogue.en: How was yesterday?

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: こうえんにいきました。ともだちとしゃしんをとりました。
dialogue.en: I went to the park. I took photos with a friend.

dialogue.speaker: friend
dialogue.ja: たのしかったですか。
dialogue.en: Was it fun?

listenCheck.question: Where did the traveller go?

responsePractice.prompt: Say that you went to a café yesterday.
choices: きのう、カフェにいきました。
きのう、カフェにいきます。
あした、カフェにいきました。
meanings: Yesterday, I went to a café.
Tomorrow, I went to a café.
responsePractice.why: ました marks a polite past action.

lessons.sayTask: Tell a partner one thing you did yesterday and one reaction to it.
lessons.adaptation: Change the place and add a second activity with と or も.

lessons.title: Add a detail to your story
lessons.goal: Add a quantity or duration when you talk about a past activity.
lessons.scene: You compare notes about a visit that lasted part of the afternoon.

dialogue.speaker: friend
dialogue.ja: どのくらいまちましたか。
dialogue.en: How long did you wait?

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: いちじかんぐらいまちました。
dialogue.en: I waited for about an hour.

dialogue.speaker: friend
dialogue.ja: わたしもたくさんしゃしんをとりました。
dialogue.en: I took lots of photos too.

listenCheck.question: How long did the traveller wait?

responsePractice.prompt: Say you took many photos too.
choices: わたしもしゃしんをたくさんとりました。
わたしはしゃしんをとります。
しゃしんはどこですか。
meanings: I took lots of photos too.
responsePractice.why: も adds “also,” and たくさん adds quantity.

lessons.sayTask: Retell a past visit and add a count, duration, or “also” detail.
lessons.adaptation: Change the activity and duration; ask your partner one follow-up.
successChecks: Adds a quantity or shared detail

learningTargets: Locate a person or thing with あります・います and a simple place relationship.
Ask and answer about a past day with polite past forms such as でした and ました.
Use も, と, たくさん, and a simple duration to add one useful detail.
Read place and time words in kana and listen for who, where, and when.

weeks.title: Describe a trip and make choices
weeks.canDo: Describe a place or item, say what you like, and invite someone to choose an activity together.

phraseBank.ja: これをひとつください。
ふたつください。
カードでおねがいします。
ふくろはいりますか。
おきなわはあたたかいです。
phraseBank.use: Describe a place with an い-adjective.

phraseBank.ja: いっしょに [ばしょ] へいきましょう。

kanaFocus: Katakana: サシスセソ・タチツテト
Katakana: ナニヌネノ・ハヒフヘホ
Read loanwords: サイズ・カード・レシート

kanjiCards.whyHere: Recognize a useful quantity form; practise saying the quantity, not handwriting the character.
Recognize a useful travel word as a whole item.

lessons.title: Describe a place
lessons.goal: Understand a simple description and say what a place is like.
lessons.scene: A friend is choosing between two places for a short trip.

dialogue.speaker: friend
dialogue.ja: おきなわはどんなところですか。
dialogue.en: What kind of place is Okinawa?

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: うみがきれいで、あたたかいところです。
dialogue.en: It is a place with a beautiful sea and warm weather.

dialogue.speaker: friend
dialogue.ja: いいですね。
dialogue.en: That sounds nice.

listenCheck.question: What is the sea like?

responsePractice.prompt: Describe a room as quiet and clean.
choices: しずかできれいなへやです。
しずかなへやをのみます。
meanings: It is a quiet, clean room.
responsePractice.why: A な-adjective can appear before a noun with な.

lessons.sayTask: Describe one place with an adjective, then add one detail about what you can see there.
lessons.adaptation: Swap the place and use a different adjective; say how it was after a visit.
successChecks: Uses an adjective with a noun

lessons.title: Share a preference
lessons.goal: Say what you like and understand a short suggestion.
lessons.scene: You and a friend are picking an activity for a day off.

dialogue.speaker: friend
dialogue.ja: どんなたべものがすきですか。
dialogue.en: What kind of food do you like?

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: あまいものがすきです。
dialogue.en: I like sweet things.

dialogue.speaker: friend
dialogue.ja: じゃあ、ケーキをふたつかいましょう。
dialogue.en: Then let’s buy two cakes.

listenCheck.question: What kind of food does the traveller like?

responsePractice.prompt: Say you like a quiet café.
choices: しずかなカフェがすきです。
しずかなカフェをすきです。
カフェはなんじですか。
responsePractice.why: 好き is commonly paired with が.

lessons.sayTask: Name one thing you like and one you do not like; a real or pretend answer is fine.
lessons.adaptation: Change the food or activity, then ask what your partner likes.
successChecks: Uses が with 好き in a model phrase

lessons.title: Suggest an activity and count
lessons.goal: Suggest a shared activity and understand a simple item count.
lessons.scene: At a market, you and a friend plan to buy a few souvenirs before heading out.

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: このおみやげをみましょうか。
dialogue.en: Shall we look at this souvenir?

dialogue.speaker: friend
dialogue.ja: いいですね。はがきをさんまいかいましょう。
dialogue.en: Good idea. Let’s buy three postcards.

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: それから、うみへいきましょう。
dialogue.en: Then let’s go to the sea.

listenCheck.question: How many postcards will they buy?

responsePractice.prompt: Suggest going to the museum together.

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: はい、あります。うみでおよぎました。
dialogue.en: Yes. I swam in the sea.

dialogue.speaker: friend
dialogue.ja: どうでしたか。
dialogue.en: How was it?

listenCheck.question: Has the traveller swum in Okinawa?

responsePractice.prompt: Say that you have never ridden a horse.
choices: うまにのったことがありません。
meanings: I have never ridden a horse.
I want to ride a horse.
responsePractice.why: たことがあります asks about a past experience.

lessons.sayTask: Ask a partner whether they have tried a familiar activity; answer truthfully or imagine an answer.
lessons.adaptation: Change the activity and add one short reaction to the experience.

lessons.title: Introduce a friend and hometown
lessons.goal: Introduce a friend and mention a few things to do in a hometown.
lessons.scene: You introduce a friend at a local gathering and compare places to visit.

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: こちらはあきさんです。メルボルンからきました。
dialogue.en: This is Aki. They are from Melbourne.

dialogue.speaker: friend
dialogue.ja: はじめまして。メルボルンにはこうえんやカフェがあります。
dialogue.en: Nice to meet you. Melbourne has parks, cafés, and other places.

dialogue.speaker: host
dialogue.ja: いいですね。
dialogue.en: That sounds nice.

listenCheck.question: Which town is mentioned?

responsePractice.prompt: Give two examples of places in your hometown.
choices: こうえんやカフェがあります。
こうえんもカフェをいきます。
どこかにいきたいです。
meanings: There are parks, cafés, and other places.
responsePractice.why: や gives a few examples without listing everything.

lessons.sayTask: Introduce a friend, then name two or three places or things in a hometown.
lessons.adaptation: Change the friend and town; ask one question about what they like doing there.

learningTargets: Express a wish with 〜たい and name a small set of activities with 〜たり〜たりする.
Ask and answer whether someone has ever done something with 〜たことがある.
Introduce a friend, ask about a hometown, and give examples with や.
Listen for whether a story is a plan, a past experience, or a list of activities.

weeks.title: Explain a health concern and respond
weeks.canDo: Describe a simple symptom, give or understand gentle advice, and say what needs to happen next.
weeks.conversationStage: recognize → supported response → adapt → communicate with less scripting

phraseBank.ja: まず、[こと] をおねがいします。
それから、[しつもん]。
もういちどおねがいします。
わかりました。ありがとうございます。
あたまがいたいんです。
くすりをのんだほうがいいです。

kanaFocus: Review learner-selected high-value kana
Read short signs, menu items, and travel prompts
No new script requirement; prioritize confident communication

kanjiCards.whyHere: Recognize a practical place word with its kana reading.
Recognize a common care-related word; no handwriting required.

milestone.title: Integrated conversation checkpoint
milestone.task: Sustain a short familiar conversation across at least three functions, including a health or help-seeking exchange, ask two follow-ups, and use one clarification or repair phrase. After a clear beginner dialogue, state its gist and key details.
evidence: Support used and next learning goal
rubric: Gets the main communicative intent across
Uses an appropriate phrase for the situation
Responds to a follow-up or changed detail
Uses clarification or repair when needed
Understands gist and key facts from clear beginner input

lessons.title: Explain a symptom
lessons.goal: Tell a helper what is wrong and understand one follow-up question.
lessons.scene: In a language-practice role-play at a clinic reception, explain a simple symptom and when it started.

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.ja: どうしましたか。
dialogue.en: What seems to be the problem?

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: あたまがいたいんです。きのうからです。
dialogue.en: I have a headache. Since yesterday.

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.ja: ねつはありますか。
dialogue.en: Do you have a fever?

listenCheck.question: What symptom does the traveller mention?

responsePractice.prompt: Explain that your throat hurts.
responsePractice.why: んです introduces a short explanation of a situation.

lessons.sayTask: Use a fictional or simple role-play symptom and add when it started.
lessons.adaptation: Change the symptom and ask one clear follow-up question; for real health needs, use qualified medical help.

lessons.title: Give gentle advice
lessons.goal: Understand a suggestion and give a simple reason for it.
lessons.scene: A friend has been very busy and says they are tired after doing too much.

dialogue.speaker: friend
dialogue.ja: きのう、べんきょうしすぎました。とてもつかれています。
dialogue.en: I studied too much yesterday. I am very tired.

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: きょうはゆっくりやすんだほうがいいです。
dialogue.en: You should take it easy and get some rest today.

dialogue.speaker: friend
dialogue.ja: そうですね。
dialogue.en: You’re right.

listenCheck.question: What does the traveller suggest?

responsePractice.prompt: Give advice to someone with a cold.
choices: びょういんへいったほうがいいです。
もっとはたらいたほうがいいです。
meanings: You should go to a hospital.
responsePractice.why: ほうがいい offers a simple suggestion; choose wording that fits the situation.

lessons.sayTask: Give one gentle suggestion for a fictional situation and say why with ので.
lessons.adaptation: Change the problem and suggestion; keep the tone caring, not forceful.

lessons.title: Plan the next step
lessons.goal: Say what needs to happen next and complete the final open-ended conversation without a fixed answer menu.
lessons.scene: Final mission: combine a greeting, one practical detail from earlier weeks, and a simple health concern in a short role-play. Use a phrase card only after you have tried.

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.ja: きょうはどうしましたか。
dialogue.en: What brings you in today?

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: ねつがあるんです。くすりをのみましたが、まだあたまがいたいです。
dialogue.en: I have a fever. I took medicine, but my head still hurts.

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.ja: きょうはやすまなければいけません。しんぱいでしたら、びょういんへいってください。
dialogue.en: You need to rest today. If you are worried, please go to a hospital.

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: わかりました。ありがとうございます。
dialogue.en: I understand. Thank you.

listenCheck.question: What does the helper say the traveller needs to do today?

responsePractice.prompt: Complete the final mission without a fixed answer menu; explain a symptom, ask for one next step, and respond to the advice in your own words.
responsePractice.why: There is no single correct sentence. Try first, then use a cue if you need one.

lessons.sayTask: Complete the role-play and note what you handled independently, with support, or want to practise next.
lessons.adaptation: Change the symptom and one earlier detail such as a time, place, or activity; keep the conversation understandable.

learningTargets: Explain a symptom or situation with 〜んです and describe that something is too much with 〜すぎる.
Give gentle advice with 〜ほうがいい and connect a reason with ので.
Say what you have to do with 〜なければいけない and ask a polite question about the next step.
Use kana-first health words and selective kanji recognition to navigate a simple care-seeking conversation.

courseAlignment: An original, independent 12-week companion aligned to the broad scope and sequence of GENKI I (Third Edition), Lessons 1–12. It uses new scenes, explanations, prompts, and dialogues; it does not reproduce textbook text, exercises, or audio and is not affiliated with the publisher.
